_comment: Single source of truth for version pins, ports, paths, and defaults shared across the npm and Docker install paths. Read by scripts/dev-safe.mjs, scripts/dev-with-automation.mjs, docker/entrypoint.sh (via generated defaults.env), and .github/workflows/docker.yml.

constraints._comment: Temporary upper bound on the agent-client-protocol (acp) transitive dependency. openhands-sdk 1.35.0 requires agent-client-protocol>=0.10.1 with no upper bound, but acp 0.11.0 reordered the ACP prompt() arguments and breaks the SDK's ACP client (a PromptRequest validation error surfaces as 'ACP error: 2 validation errors for PromptRequest'). Pin acp <0.11 until a fixed openhands-sdk ships. Consumed by scripts/dev-safe.mjs (agent-server uvx install) and .github/workflows/mock-llm-e2e.yml (mock ACP server venv).
constraints._fastmcpComment: Bounds on the fastmcp transitive dependency, which owns MCP OAuth token refresh and the authorization callback. openhands-sdk declares 'fastmcp>=3.0.0' with no ceiling, so a fresh uvx install resolves fastmcp 4.x / mcp 2.x. Both ends of the unbounded range break OAuth MCP servers (Atlassian Rovo, GitLab): fastmcp <3.2.0 never loads the persisted token expiry, so is_token_valid() returns True for an expired access token, the refresh grant is skipped and the stale token is sent; fastmcp >=4 switched callback_handler() to return an AuthorizationCodeResult, so the agent-server's callback fork raises "'tuple' object has no attribute 'state'" and re-authorization fails. Hold fastmcp in the range that does both correctly until an SDK ships with its own ceiling. Docker is unaffected (the SDK image builds from uv.lock). Consumed by scripts/dev-safe.mjs (agent-server uvx install). See OpenHands/OpenHands#17077 and OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#4818.

ports._vscodeComment: Port the bundled editor binds to inside the container; agent-server's own default. Only the Docker entrypoint reads this — the npm launchers derive the editor port from the agent-server port so several stacks can run side by side. It is never published: the editor is reached through paths.vscodeBasePath on the proxy port.

paths._vscodeBasePathComment: Path prefix the bundled editor is served under, on the same origin as the canvas. Passed to agent-server as OH_VSCODE_BASE_PATH (it launches openvscode-server with --server-base-path and advertises the prefix in /api/vscode/url), and registered as an ingress route to the VSCode port. Keeping one value on both sides is what lets a single-origin deployment reach the editor without publishing a second port. Tradeoff: a path prefix routes but does not isolate, so the editor shares the canvas's browser origin and therefore its localStorage — see docs/SELF_HOSTING.md and OpenHands/OpenHands#16492.
